videos.script: Two more tools, and they could hardly be more different. {{haystack}} Haystack builds a pipeline out of components with typed inputs and outputs, and it refuses to connect two that do not fit, before anything runs. {{ids}} Its ids are hashes of the content and the metadata. Load the same text twice and it refuses. Change one metadata field, and the same chunk goes in a second time. {{floor}} Lesson 6's floor becomes a component of its own, with two outputs: the documents, or the refusal. The duplicate shows up in the answer, as two sources that are one. {{yaml}} And the whole pipeline can be written out as a file, with the key as the name of a variable rather than the key itself. {{measure}} Its default splitter is the most sensible of the frameworks so far. {{ragflow}} RAGFlow is not a library at all. It is a server application, built around reading difficult documents, with a screen where people can see and correct the chunks. {{choose}} Five ways to build the same thing. The test, the filters and the decisions stay the same whichever you choose. {{end}}
